name: coverage-interpretation
title: Coverage and Network Interpretation
summary: Read coverage evidence into a CoverageResult, keeping 'accepts this insurance' separate from 'in network for this plan' and resolving every gap to unknown.
when_to_use: The workflow is in COVERAGE_CHECK and a CoverageResult is needed for a plan
A provider or hospital has just been chosen and a provider-level network check is required
Two coverage sources disagree about network status and the disagreement must be surfaced
A patient asks whether a visit is covered and the answer must be a network status, not a guarantee

inputs.name: plan
inputs.description: The plan being checked. Its plan_type and network_name shape what a network record can mean.

inputs.name: plan_id
inputs.description: Identifier of the plan under check; always required, provider optional.

inputs.name: evidence
inputs.description: Structured coverage responses and descriptive text. Structured evidence outranks descriptive.

inputs.name: provider_id
inputs.description: Present only after a provider is known; a provider-level check must not run before then.

inputs.name: hospital_id
inputs.description: Optional facility scope for the network question.

outputs.name: coverage
outputs.description: accepts_insurance, in_network_for_plan, status, referral_required, prior_auth_required, freshness, evidence.

outputs.name: conflict
outputs.type: {conflict: boolean, conflicting_evidence_ids: EvidenceId[], winning_evidence_id: EvidenceId | null}
outputs.description: Set when sources disagree: the structured result wins and the disagreement is reported, not smoothed over.

outputs.name: decision
outputs.description: Reason code is ok, coverage_unknown, provider_not_in_network, stale_evidence or conflicting_evidence.

references.purpose: A short worked example of the structured-versus-descriptive conflict, showing what is reported and what is refused.
